REGIONAL REGULATION OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN CITY

NUMBER 3 OF 2021

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, therefore regulation is needed as a basis for implementing comprehensive and integrated protection of women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Padang Sidempuan City; In View of:

1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1984 Number 29, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3277); 3. Law Number 5 of 1998 concerning Ratification of the Convention Against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1998 Number 164, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3783); 4. Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1999 Number 165, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3886); 5. CHAPTER VI

FORMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 10

Forms of violence include:
a. physical violence;
b. psychological violence;
c. sexual violence; and/or
d. domestic neglect.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Padang Sidempuan. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Mayor is the Mayor of Padang Sidempuan. 5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD of Padang Sidempuan City is a Regional People's Representative Institution which is positioned as an element of Regional Government Administration. 6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the region. 7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 8. Women Empowerment and Child Protection System is the entire process of organizing women empowerment and child protection carried out comprehensively, inclusively, and integratively starting from the stage of report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, up to repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of crime and violence to their social environment. 9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 11. Victim is a person who suffers physical, mental, and/or economic loss caused by a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that causes injury or death to another person or causes physical damage or property of another person. 13. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences violence and/or suffering as a result of violence and/or threat of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children and among people who are in their dependents. 18. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to the area of origin. 20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 21. Prevention is a direct effort made by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 23. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards. 24. Child-Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 25. Child-friendly city task force hereinafter abbreviated as KLA task force is a coordinative institution at the city level that coordinates policies, programs and activities to realize KLA. 29. Business Entity is an institution that daily carries out activities to seek profit and gain, but has a commitment to the protection of women and children. 26. Business Entity is an institution that daily carries out activities to seek profit and gain, but has a commitment to the protection of women and children
27. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live properly and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 28. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies. 29.

Article 11

Physical violence as referred to in Article 10 letter a results in:
a. the victim becomes ill or seriously injured;
b. the death of the victim; and
c. causes disease or impediment to carrying out work, position or livelihood or daily activities.

Article 13

Sexual violence as referred to in Article 10 letter c is in the form of:
a. acts of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
c. coercion of sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

CHAPTER XVI

COOPERATION

Article 45

1. Regional cooperation is joint effort between regions with other regions, between regions with third parties, and/or between regions and institutions or regional governments abroad based on a balance of efficiency and effectiveness of public services and mutual benefit.
2. Regional cooperation with third parties, hereinafter abbreviated as KSDPK, is joint effort carried out by regions with third parties in the context of implementing governmental affairs that are regional authority to improve community welfare and accelerate the fulfillment of public services.
3. In order to achieve the objectives of protecting the rights of women and children from acts of violence, the regional government cooperates with:
a. other provinces;
b. regencies/cities; and
c. non-governmental institutions.
4. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (3) includes:
a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses which are followed up in accordance with applicable law.

Article 7

1. The obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process against cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) are based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.
3. The obligations and responsibilities of the community towards child protection are implemented through community role activities in the implementation of child protection.
4. The obligations and responsibilities of the community towards child protection are implemented through community role activities in the implementation of child protection.
5. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in paragraph (4) are implemented by involving community organizations, academics, and child observers.  ­

Article 18

1. Health Services are provided by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector, by providing treatment and health recovery services for victims.
2. Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims.
3. Counseling is provided by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
4. Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
5. Victim resocialization is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

CHAPTER XII

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 30

In the context of implementing the Protection of Women and Children, the following are established:
a. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A);
b. Family Welfare Consultation Institution; and
c. Other institutions in accordance with needs and/or provisions of statutory regulations.

CHAPTER XVIII

CRIMINAL PROVISIONS

Article 48

Any person who commits a criminal act/violence as referred to in Article 11, Article 12, Article 13, and Article 14 shall be threatened with criminal punishment in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

a. physical violence;
b. psychological violence;
c. sexual violence; and/or

c. prevent violations of women's rights in the household.

b. regencies/cities; and

Article 20

3\. basic health and welfare;
4\. education, leisure time and cultural activities;and
5\. special protection.

b. psychological violence;
c. sexual violence; and/or

Article 45

1. Regional cooperation is joint effort between regions with other regions, between regions with third parties, and/or between regions and institutions or regional governments abroad based on a balance of efficiency and effectiveness of public services and mutual benefit.

a. exchange of data and information;

Article 18

5. Victim resocialization is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

CHAPTER XI

CHILDREN'S FORUM

Article 28

1. The Regional Government is obliged to establish a children's forum at the Padang Sidempuan City level as participation through the children's forum.
2. The children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) represents children, both representation of children's geographical domicile, components of children's socio-cultural groups and children's educational background and accommodates the interests of children with special needs.
3. In every formulation of policies related to children, the Regional Government must consider and accommodate the opinions of children conveyed through the children's forum.
4. The establishment of the children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Mayor's Decree.
5. Sources of funding for the implementation of children's forum activities may come from:
a. contributions from members of the children's forum;  ­
b. donations from the community/private parties that are legal and non-binding;
c. assistance from the City Government; and/ord. other sources of funding in accordance with statutory regulations.

Article 7

1. The obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process against cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) are based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.
3. The obligations and responsibilities of the community towards child protection are implemented through community role activities in the implementation of child protection.
4. The obligations and responsibilities of the community towards child protection are implemented through community role activities in the implementation of child protection.
5. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in paragraph (4) are implemented by involving community organizations, academics, and child observers.  ­

CHAPTER XIV

FUNDING

Article 43

1. The Regional Government is obligated to provide a budget for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs and activities.
2. Financing for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection activities as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD); and
b. other legal and non-binding sources based on the provisions of laws and regulations.

3.6.text:
Article 18

1. Health Services are provided by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector, by providing treatment and health recovery services for victims.
2. Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims.
3. Counseling is provided by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
4. Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
5. Victim resocialization is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

CHAPTER XVI

COOPERATION

Article 45

1. Regional cooperation is joint effort between regions with other regions, between regions with third parties, and/or between regions and institutions or regional governments abroad based on a balance of efficiency and effectiveness of public services and mutual benefit.
2. Regional cooperation with third parties, hereinafter abbreviated as KSDPK, is joint effort carried out by regions with third parties in the context of implementing governmental affairs that are regional authority to improve community welfare and accelerate the fulfillment of public services.

a. other provinces;
b. regencies/cities; and
c. non-governmental institutions.

a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses which are followed up in accordance with applicable law.

a. an information center for women and children;  ­
b. a service center for women and victims of violence; and
c. an empowerment center for women and children.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN CITY

NUMBER 3 OF 2021

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, therefore regulation is needed as a basis for implementing comprehensive and integrated protection of women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Padang Sidempuan City; In View of:

1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1984 Number 29, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3277); 3. CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, therefore regulation is needed as a basis for implementing comprehensive and integrated protection of women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Padang Sidempuan City; In View of:

1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1984 Number 29, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3277); 3. Law Number 5 of 1998 concerning Ratification of the Convention Against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1998 Number 164, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3783); 4. Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1999 Number 165, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3886); 5. Article 12

Part Four

Obligations of the Family

Article 34

The Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment and Protection (P2TP2A) functions as:
a. an information center for women and children;  ­
b. a service center for women and victims of violence; and
c. an empowerment center for women and children.

CHAPTER XVI

COOPERATION

Article 45

1. Regional cooperation is joint effort between regions with other regions, between regions with third parties, and/or between regions and institutions or regional governments abroad based on a balance of efficiency and effectiveness of public services and mutual benefit.
2. Regional cooperation with third parties, hereinafter abbreviated as KSDPK, is joint effort carried out by regions with third parties in the context of implementing governmental affairs that are regional authority to improve community welfare and accelerate the fulfillment of public services.
3. In order to achieve the objectives of protecting the rights of women and children from acts of violence, the regional government cooperates with:
a. other provinces;
b. regencies/cities; and
c. non-governmental institutions.
4. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (3) includes:
a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses which are followed up in accordance with applicable law.

Article 11

Physical violence as referred to in Article 10 letter a results in:
a. the victim becomes ill or seriously injured;
b. the death of the victim; and
c. causes disease or impediment to carrying out work, position or livelihood or daily activities.

Obligations of the Community

OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 30

a. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A);
b. Family Welfare Consultation Institution; and
c. Other institutions in accordance with needs and/or provisions of statutory regulations.

Article 8

The family in efforts to protect the rights of women is obliged to:
a. protect women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent violations of women's rights in the household.

Part Two

Obligations of Regional Government

3.9.text:
Article 18

1. Health Services are provided by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector, by providing treatment and health recovery services for victims.
2. Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims.
3. Counseling is provided by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
4. Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
5. Victim resocialization is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Padang Sidempuan. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Mayor is the Mayor of Padang Sidempuan. 5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD of Padang Sidempuan City is a Regional People's Representative Institution which is positioned as an element of Regional Government Administration. 6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the region. 7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 8. Women Empowerment and Child Protection System is the entire process of organizing women empowerment and child protection carried out comprehensively, inclusively, and integratively starting from the stage of report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, up to repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of crime and violence to their social environment. 9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 11. Victim is a person who suffers physical, mental, and/or economic loss caused by a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that causes injury or death to another person or causes physical damage or property of another person. 13. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children and among people who are in their dependents. 18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to the area of origin. 20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 21. Prevention is a direct effort made by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 23. Child-friendly city task force hereinafter abbreviated as KLA task force is a coordinative institution at the city level that coordinates policies, programs and activities to realize KLA. 29. Business Entity is an institution that daily carries out activities to seek profit and gain, but has a commitment to the protection of women and children. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the regional government or community-based, which includes: referral center, business consultation center, reproductive health consultation center, legal consultation center, integrated crisis center (PKT), integrated service center (PPT), trauma recovery center (trauma center), women crisis center, training center, science and technology information center (PIPTEK), safe house (shelter), transit house, children's friend telephone (TESA) 129, or other forms.

Article 36

The Family Learning Center (PUSPAGA) is a form of preventive service under the coordination of the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as a manifestation of state concern in improving family life and family resilience through education or parenting programs, parenting skills, child protection skills, ability to increase child participation in the family as well as counseling program services for children and families.

Article 35

1. The Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment and Protection (P2TP2A) at City Level shall be established based on a Mayor Decree and a Sub-District Head Decree for the sub-district level.
2. Membership of the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment and Protection (P2TP2A) may come from elements of regional apparatus, professional organizations, academics, community leaders and other elements as needed.
3. Further provisions regarding P2TP2A shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

CHAPTER XI

CHILDREN'S FORUM

Article 28

1. The Regional Government is obliged to establish a children's forum at the Padang Sidempuan City level as participation through the children's forum.
2. The children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) represents children, both representation of children's geographical domicile, components of children's socio-cultural groups and children's educational background and accommodates the interests of children with special needs.
3. In every formulation of policies related to children, the Regional Government must consider and accommodate the opinions of children conveyed through the children's forum.
4. The establishment of the children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Mayor's Decree.
5. Sources of funding for the implementation of children's forum activities may come from:
a. contributions from members of the children's forum;  ­
b. donations from the community/private parties that are legal and non-binding;
c. assistance from the City Government; and/ord. other sources of funding in accordance with statutory regulations.

Article 37

CHAPTER XVI

COOPERATION

Article 45

1. Regional cooperation is joint effort between regions with other regions, between regions with third parties, and/or between regions and institutions or regional governments abroad based on a balance of efficiency and effectiveness of public services and mutual benefit.
2. Regional cooperation with third parties, hereinafter abbreviated as KSDPK, is joint effort carried out by regions with third parties in the context of implementing governmental affairs that are regional authority to improve community welfare and accelerate the fulfillment of public services.
3. In order to achieve the objectives of protecting the rights of women and children from acts of violence, the regional government cooperates with:
a. other provinces;
b. regencies/cities; and
c. non-governmental institutions.
4. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (3) includes:
a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses which are followed up in accordance with applicable law.

Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the regional government or community-based, which includes: referral center, business consultation center, reproductive health consultation center, legal consultation center, integrated crisis center (PKT), integrated service center (PPT), trauma recovery center (trauma center), women crisis center, training center, science and technology information center (PIPTEK), safe house (shelter), transit house, children's friend telephone (TESA) 129, or other forms.

Article 13

Sexual violence as referred to in Article 10 letter c is in the form of:
a. acts of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
c. coercion of sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

CHAPTER VI

FORMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 10

Forms of violence include:
a. physical violence;
b. psychological violence;
c. sexual violence; and/or
d. domestic neglect.

CHAPTER XVIII

CRIMINAL PROVISIONS

Article 48

Any person who commits a criminal act/violence as referred to in Article 11, Article 12, Article 13, and Article 14 shall be threatened with criminal punishment in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 18

1. Health Services are provided by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector, by providing treatment and health recovery services for victims.
2. Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims.
3. Counseling is provided by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
4. Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
5. Victim resocialization is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

CHAPTER XIV

FUNDING

Article 43

1. The Regional Government is obligated to provide a budget for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs and activities.
2. Financing for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection activities as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD); and
b. other legal and non-binding sources based on the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 34

The Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment and Protection (P2TP2A) functions as:
a. an information center for women and children;  ­
b. a service center for women and victims of violence; and
c. an empowerment center for women and children.

CHAPTER XV

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 44

1. The community may participate in the implementation of women's empowerment activities.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, community groups and community organizations.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. cooperation;
b. active role in policy formulation; and
c. complaints/reports.
4. The procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

CHAPTERX

INFORMATION SYSTEM FOR DATA ON WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 20

1. An information system is a system for collecting, preparing, storing, processing, analyzing and/or disseminating information.
2. The Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of gender and child data consisting of components-components-components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/agencies and regions in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of development that is gender responsive and child-friendly.
3. Gender Data is data regarding the relationship of relations in status, roles and conditions between men and women.
4. Disaggregated Data is data disaggregated by sex, age, status and condition of women in all fields of development including health, education, economy and employment, politics and decision-making, law and socio-culture and violence.
5. Types of gender and child data:
a. gender data:
1\. gender data in the economic field including gender issues in labor, cooperatives, small and medium enterprises, industry and trade, agriculture, forestry, fisheries and marine affairs, transportation, science and technology and infrastructure;
2\. gender data in the political, social and legal fields;
3\. data on protection of women's rights; and
4\. data on family welfare and resilience development.
b. child data:
1\. civil rights and freedoms;
2\. family environment and alternative care;
3\. basic health and welfare;
4\. education, leisure time and cultural activities;and
5\. special protection.
6. Gender analysis is the process of analyzing disaggregated data by sex conducted systematically with the intention of identifying gender issues and factors that can influence development, particularly related to gender equality issues that are the goals of development.

Article 20

1. An information system is a system for collecting, preparing, storing, processing, analyzing and/or disseminating information.

The Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of gender and child data consisting of components-components-components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/agencies and regions in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of development that is gender responsive and child-friendly.

b. child data:

2\. family environment and alternative care;
3\. basic health and welfare;
4\. education, leisure time and cultural activities;and

INFORMATION SYSTEM FOR DATA ON WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 20

1. An information system is a system for collecting, preparing, storing, processing, analyzing and/or disseminating information.
2. The Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of gender and child data consisting of components-components-components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/agencies and regions in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of development that is gender responsive and child-friendly.
3. Gender Data is data regarding the relationship of relations in status, roles and conditions between men and women.
4. Disaggregated Data is data disaggregated by sex, age, status and condition of women in all fields of development including health, education, economy and employment, politics and decision-making, law and socio-culture and violence.
5. Types of gender and child data:
a. gender data:
1\. gender data in the economic field including gender issues in labor, cooperatives, small and medium enterprises, industry and trade, agriculture, forestry, fisheries and marine affairs, transportation, science and technology and infrastructure;
2\. gender data in the political, social and legal fields;
3\. data on protection of women's rights; and
4\. data on family welfare and resilience development.
b. child data:
1\. civil rights and freedoms;
2\. family environment and alternative care;
3\. basic health and welfare;
4\. education, leisure time and cultural activities;and
5\. special protection.
6. Gender analysis is the process of analyzing disaggregated data by sex conducted systematically with the intention of identifying gender issues and factors that can influence development, particularly related to gender equality issues that are the goals of development.

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN,

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, therefore regulation is needed as a basis for implementing comprehensive and integrated protection of women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Padang Sidempuan City; In View of:

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN CITY

NUMBER 3 OF 2021

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, therefore regulation is needed as a basis for implementing comprehensive and integrated protection of women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Padang Sidempuan City; In View of:

INFORMATION SYSTEM FOR DATA ON WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 20

1. An information system is a system for collecting, preparing, storing, processing, analyzing and/or disseminating information.
2. The Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of gender and child data consisting of components-components-components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/agencies and regions in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of development that is gender responsive and child-friendly.
3. Gender Data is data regarding the relationship of relations in status, roles and conditions between men and women.
4. Disaggregated Data is data disaggregated by sex, age, status and condition of women in all fields of development including health, education, economy and employment, politics and decision-making, law and socio-culture and violence.
5. Types of gender and child data:
a. gender data:
1\. gender data in the economic field including gender issues in labor, cooperatives, small and medium enterprises, industry and trade, agriculture, forestry, fisheries and marine affairs, transportation, science and technology and infrastructure;
2\. gender data in the political, social and legal fields;
3\. data on protection of women's rights; and
4\. data on family welfare and resilience development.
b. child data:
1\. civil rights and freedoms;
2\. family environment and alternative care;
3\. basic health and welfare;
4\. education, leisure time and cultural activities;and
5\. special protection.
6. Gender analysis is the process of analyzing disaggregated data by sex conducted systematically with the intention of identifying gender issues and factors that can influence development, particularly related to gender equality issues that are the goals of development.

CHAPTER XVI

COOPERATION

Article 45

1. Regional cooperation is joint effort between regions with other regions, between regions with third parties, and/or between regions and institutions or regional governments abroad based on a balance of efficiency and effectiveness of public services and mutual benefit.
2. Regional cooperation with third parties, hereinafter abbreviated as KSDPK, is joint effort carried out by regions with third parties in the context of implementing governmental affairs that are regional authority to improve community welfare and accelerate the fulfillment of public services.
3. In order to achieve the objectives of protecting the rights of women and children from acts of violence, the regional government cooperates with:
a. other provinces;
b. regencies/cities; and
c. non-governmental institutions.

a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses which are followed up in accordance with applicable law.

FUNDING

CHAPTER XVI

COOPERATION

Article 45

1. Regional cooperation is joint effort between regions with other regions, between regions with third parties, and/or between regions and institutions or regional governments abroad based on a balance of efficiency and effectiveness of public services and mutual benefit.
2. Regional cooperation with third parties, hereinafter abbreviated as KSDPK, is joint effort carried out by regions with third parties in the context of implementing governmental affairs that are regional authority to improve community welfare and accelerate the fulfillment of public services.
3. In order to achieve the objectives of protecting the rights of women and children from acts of violence, the regional government cooperates with:
a. other provinces;
b. regencies/cities; and
c. non-governmental institutions.
4. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (3) includes:
a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses which are followed up in accordance with applicable law.

Article 18

1. Health Services are provided by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector, by providing treatment and health recovery services for victims.
2. Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims.
3. Counseling is provided by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
4. Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
5. Victim resocialization is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

Article 20

b. child data:

CHAPTERX

INFORMATION SYSTEM FOR DATA ON WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 20

1. An information system is a system for collecting, preparing, storing, processing, analyzing and/or disseminating information.
2. The Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of gender and child data consisting of components-components-components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/agencies and regions in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of development that is gender responsive and child-friendly.
3. Gender Data is data regarding the relationship of relations in status, roles and conditions between men and women.
4. Disaggregated Data is data disaggregated by sex, age, status and condition of women in all fields of development including health, education, economy and employment, politics and decision-making, law and socio-culture and violence.
5. Types of gender and child data:
a. gender data:
1\. gender data in the economic field including gender issues in labor, cooperatives, small and medium enterprises, industry and trade, agriculture, forestry, fisheries and marine affairs, transportation, science and technology and infrastructure;
2\. gender data in the political, social and legal fields;
3\. data on protection of women's rights; and
4\. data on family welfare and resilience development.
b. child data:
1\. civil rights and freedoms;
2\. family environment and alternative care;
3\. basic health and welfare;
4\. education, leisure time and cultural activities;and
5\. special protection.
6. Gender analysis is the process of analyzing disaggregated data by sex conducted systematically with the intention of identifying gender issues and factors that can influence development, particularly related to gender equality issues that are the goals of development.
